video.title: Nayab Aur Manhar Ki Mehfil | UK & EUROPE TOUR ANNOUNCEMENT

emotional.video_read: A staged poetry evening: a host brings poet Nayab Mida up on stage and the two trade verse for several minutes — her own shayari (ishq vs pyaar, the Shahjahan/Taj Mahal piece, a Bashir Badr sher), a recitation of 'Muskurao', a Rahat Indori ghazal, and her parting words to the heartbroken. Nearly all the emotional material lives in the recited verse from roughly the two-minute mark to the end; the first ninety seconds is a tour announcement and the guest introduction.

near_misses.why_not: Opens on a garbled host interjection ('जब मैं छोटी थी तो ये बात मेरे मां-बाप को नहीं पता थी') that points at a story never told; the thought she actually completes begins one line later.
Host praising the recitation and requesting the next poem — commentary on emotion, not the thing itself.
Host joke riffing on the glass-half-empty line ('there is always room for sharab') — comedy, and it only works with the poem just heard.

clips.title: ताजमहल तो बनवा लोगे, मुमताज़ कहाँ से?
clips.description: A complete recited piece that turns the Taj Mahal inside out: Shahjahan cut off the builders' hands so no one could tell his love story better — and the closing line asks where you'll find a Mumtaz, even if you can still commission the Taj. Ends on the punchline before the host's reaction begins.
clips.boundary_note: Dropped opening 'और' (connective to the preceding praise) and started on the sher's own first words 'मैंने सुना है'; kept the proposed end at 'मुमताज कहां से' and excluded the trailing 'आय हाय क्या बात' host reaction so the piece lands clean.

step1.title: ताजमहल तो बनवा लोगे, मुमताज़ कहाँ से?
step1.why: The strongest thing in the video. It takes the world's most famous monument of love and turns it inside out: Shahjahan had the hands of the Taj's builders cut off 'so no one could build above his ishq, no one could tell his love story better' — the audience suddenly sees possessiveness where it expected devotion. Then the last line lands and leaves: you can still commission a Taj Mahal, but where will you find a Mumtaz? A complete piece with one written ending, a measured pause to settle after it, replay data and multiple viewer comments marking it. Slow delivery on the turn (L0034) is visible in the tags.

clips.title: मुस्कुराओ — उस जीत की ज़रूरत तुमसे ज़्यादा किसी को थी शायद
clips.description: The complete 'Muskurao' recitation, from its opening refrain to the final spoken 'मुस्कुराओ' before the long pause. A closed poem about meeting defeat, loss and a half-empty glass with a smile — it only resolves at the last refrain, so it ships whole.

segments.start_words: मुस्कुराओ मुस्कुराओ अगर आज कहीं से हार गए हो
segments.text: मुस्कुराओ मुस्कुराओ अगर आज कहीं से हार गए हो। उस जीत की जरूरत तुमसे ज्यादा किसी को थी शायद। मुस्कुराओ अगर कुछ खो गया है। जिसके नसीब का था उसको मिल गया है शायद। मुस्कुराओ अगर दिल टूट गया है। किसी का जोड़ने के लिए किसी का तोड़ना पड़ता होगा शायद। और फिर भी रह जाए अगर दिल में दर्द कहीं तो बांट कर मुस्कुराओ। और है अगर दिल में खुशी ज्यादा तो सेम प्रोसेस दोहराओ। मुस्कुराओ अगर सर पर है छत बदन पर है कपड़ा और है थाली में खाना और है अगर जरूरत से ज्यादा तो बांट कर घर जाना। मुस्कुराओ जब बार-बार यह सोच कर हताश हो जाते हो कि इससे अच्छा यह हो जाता, इससे अच्छा वो हो जाता। तब यह सोच कर मुस्कुराओ कि इससे बुरा हो जाता तो क्या हो जाता। मुस्कुराओ जब पूछे कोई कि जिंदगी जीने का है क्या सलीका। मुस्कुराओ यह कह कर कि हमने जिंदगी से मुस्कुराना ही सीखा। मुस्कुराओ। वो दुनिया जो तुमसे पूछती रहती है ना ग्लास तुम आधा खाली देखते हो, भरा देखते हो। मुस्कुराओ इवन इफ यू हैव टू वर्क माइल्स एंड माइल्स बिकॉज़ इट्स ओके इफ द ग्लास इज हाफ एम्प्टी यू कैन ऑलवेज ऑलवेज फिल इट विथ स्माइल्स। मुस्कुराओ।

step1.title: मुस्कुराओ — उस जीत की ज़रूरत तुमसे ज़्यादा किसी को थी शायद
step1.why: The complete 'Muskurao' poem, whole — it is a closed form with a refrain that only resolves at the final 'मुस्कुराओ', so no fragment of it is shippable. Several verses do real work: 'us jeet ki zaroorat tumse zyada kisi ko thi shayad' takes a defeat away from you, and 'kisi ka jodne ke liye kisi ka todna padta hoga shayad' is a genuine reframe. The middle-to-late verses drift toward gratitude, and the glass-half-empty stretch is the flattest part of the piece — ship it anyway, because a poem that stops halfway is worse than a flat verse inside one that resolves. Long, roughly 68 seconds; the editor stage can trim edge fat but not the form.

clips.title: इश्क और प्यार एक ही तो बात है — एक दिन है और एक रात
clips.description: A complete, self-contained sher: ishq and pyaar are the same thing, the only difference is that one is day and one is night, and junoon decides that distance. Viewers quote it verbatim in the comments — the couplet carries everything a stranger needs from its first word.
clips.boundary_note: Moved the start forward from the proposal's opening ("हमें लगता है यही है...") because that sentence begins mid-thought in L0027 and is setup, not the sher. Starting on "कहा है कि इश्क और प्यार..." is a clean, non-referring opening; kept the proposed end, which lands on the sher's final line before the applause row.

clips.title: कि मेरे अपने मुझे मिट्टी में मिलाने आए
clips.description: Rahat Indori's ghazal taken whole: from the framing line 'जब आप अपने lowest पे होते हो ना, तो आपको असलियत पता लगती है कि कौन तुम्हारा सच्चा दोस्त है' through the recitation to its true closing line 'मुंतज़िर हूं कि कोई मुझे बुलाने आए'. The setup sentence is what tells a stranger whose words these are and why they hurt; the ghazal is a closed form and ends where the poet ended it.
clips.boundary_note: Moved the start back from L0055 to the word 'राहत' at the end of L0052: the proposed opening 'कि मेरे अपने...' is mid-sentence (it continues 'लिखा था कि...') and opens on a connective; starting at 'राहत' takes the whole framing sentence 'राहत इंदौरी साहब की एक यह ग़ज़ल है...' which names the poet and supplies the setup. step1.title: जो इंसान जा रहा है, उससे वो प्रेम वापस लेना
step1.why: Her parting words to the heartbroken, and they are not the usual blessing: the person leaving takes nothing from you but your fights — what you must take back is the love you gave them, because it was your investment and it is yours. That inversion (grief as an asset to reclaim, not a debt owed to someone gone) is a hard truth told with the speaker standing beside the viewer, and it ends on her own sher refusing to trade her love even if stabbed in the back. Straddles advice and emotion; the emotion dominates. The sher in L0066–L0067 is garbled in the transcript but the audio carries it. Replay-marked twice.
